title: Belmont News post front matter
description: Validates the YAML front matter block of every post file under content/YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD/. The single source of truth for field-level validation. index.mjs reads this file and additionally enforces the repo gates that a single file cannot express: path shape, folder date equals date, byline matches the roster slug, slug uniqueness, and column ownership.

date.description: Publication day in America/New_York. Must equal the day folder in the path.

edition.description: Which edition this post belongs to.

column.description: Required by the index.mjs gate when edition is column. Must be a column owned by the byline in roster.json. A column has exactly one owner, so two roster entries must not list the same column.

byline.description: Full name exactly as registered in roster.json, capitalisation included. No shared bylines. The one desk line is 'Belmont News staff', for copy no single reporter files; it is not a substitute for a reporter's name. An entry marked retired in roster.json is archive-only: the gate refuses it for any post dated after its retirement day.

slug.description: URL slug, unique across the archive. The site URL is /<date>/<slug>/.

expires.description: Optional. The newsroom day, America/New_York, on which this post stops being listed on the site's rolling front page and in feed.xml. A plain calendar day and nothing else: a time of day is refused, because the newsroom changes offset on 2026-11-01 and a rule that picked one would be right for half the year. Omit this field and the post is listed for the two newsroom days counting its own, which is the site default and needs no field. This is a listing rule only: the post's own page stays live, stays at HTTP 200, keeps its sources, and stays in sitemap.xml after it expires. Expiring a listing is not a withdrawal and does not make any claim in the copy true. index.mjs additionally checks that this day is not before the post's own date.

eventEnds.description: Optional, and a real date the post's subject actually ended on. Day granularity: the day the event, opening period, forecast period, or deadline window THIS POST DESCRIBES ended. "Closes Sunday" does not go here; 2026-10-04 does. Not relative, never "now", never an empty string: a value the schema cannot parse is a schema error, not a judgement call. Omitting it is a complete and correct answer and is never a reason to reject a draft - a desk note, a correction of record, a profile and most weather background describe something that has no end, and forcing an end date onto them would be a fiction in a field whose only job is to be true. This is NOT the same concept as expires above: expires is when the post leaves the site's listing window, which is DEFAULT_LISTING_DAYS in EasySchedule/belmont-news-site and has nothing to do with what the story is about. This field is a fact for the reviewer, not a waiver: a post carrying it passes QA under exactly the same rule as any other post. After publication it is changed by a correction, never by a silent edit. Ruled on BEL-317 (Mara Vance).

quotedTokens.description: Optional. One entry per occurrence of a time-anchored word in THIS POST that the human pass has judged to be quoted or dated source text rather than Belmont News copy, so that scripts/tense-scan.mjs does not report it. The scan reports candidates and never refuses anything; this list only decides which of its reports a human has already adjudicated. Three rules, all of them load-bearing. (1) One entry per OCCURRENCE, and context is required: it is the verbatim substring of the line the word sits on, so an entry covers that occurrence and the same word elsewhere in the post is still reported. A bare list of words says "this word is fine somewhere in here", which is wide enough to walk a real defect through. (2) reason is required, and it names the dated source the exemption rests on. An entry without a reason is not an allowance. (3) The scan skips front matter and fenced code, and implements NO structural exemption: the archive has three block-quote lines in total, all of them a street address, and the authorised-looking National Weather Service hit is our own prose labelling a period OUTSIDE the quotation marks, so a structural skip would not have exempted it anyway. This is not self-certifying. A post that declares an allowance and whose sentence turns out not to be quoted from a dated source is a returned post, the same as a fabrication. Ruled on BEL-316 (Tobias Nkemelu); the required reason on BEL-317 (Mara Vance).

token.description: The exact time-anchored word as it appears in the body, spelled the way the post spells it. It must be one of the words in the QA list on BEL-162; the scan matches it case-insensitively.

context.description: The verbatim substring of the line the word sits on, so this entry exempts one occurrence and not the word. Copied from the body, not retyped.

reason.description: Why this occurrence is attribution and not our copy: the named source, its product or document, and the date it was issued or retrieved. "It reads fine" is not a reason.

sources.description: At least one source is required. An unsourced post fails the build.

type.description: document = on-record document. human = named human source, on the record.

title.description: Document title, or the person's name when type is human.

organization.description: Issuing body, or the person's affiliation when type is human.

corrections.description: Published corrections. A correction is appended, never a silent edit.
